page: Amazon Web Services g6e.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for graphics-intensive and machine learning workloads. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.4 GHz, this instance provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It features 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The hardware configuration includes a dedicated NVIDIA L40S GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture with 45 GB of VRAM, alongside 450 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core results placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and general system benchmarks like Geekbench and Passmark fall into the average range. A notable hardware tradeoff is the memory bandwidth for large blocks, where both read and write operations for 256 MB blocks score in the bottom 25%. Conversely, the instance excels in LLM inference, achieving top-tier performance in the top 10% for prompt processing and text generation on small and medium models, as well as strong performance for large model prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g6e.2xlarge offers high resource density by bundling a high-capacity 45 GB VRAM GPU with local NVMe storage and a balanced CPU-to-RAM ratio. This makes it a cost-effective choice for specialized deployments where GPU memory and local storage speed are prioritized over raw system memory bandwidth. The instance is highly suited for workloads such as large language model inference, graphics rendering, 3D visualization, and machine learning model development.

The g6e.2xlarge is suited for workloads such as large language model inference, machine learning, and graphics-intensive applications.
